sources.entry: One Sure-Fire Way to Improve Your Coding: reading code!

summary.title: One sure-fire way to improve your coding
summary.one_liner: Reading other people's open-source code, chosen and studied deliberately, is one of the fastest ways to improve your programming skills.
keywords: learn programming by reading source code
small projects for beginners reading code
takeaways: Read code you already rely on, such as plugins or libraries, since you already know their public APIs.
Pick code that impresses you or was written by a developer you respect, and prefer small projects you can hold in your head.
Start by mapping the project's file structure and big picture before diving into details.
Read tests first to learn the author's intent, then get the suite running and experiment by breaking and changing code.
Document your findings in comments as you go, and repeat with new codebases; GitHub is a good place to find them.
summary.summary: The author argues that reading other people's code is the most reliable way to become a better programmer, and gives practical guidance on what to read. He recommends starting with code you already use, code that impresses you, or code by respected developers, and choosing small projects over large ones like Rails or Drupal. For how to read, he suggests mapping the project structure first, annotating code with comments, using the test suite to understand intent, and experimenting by changing the code. The piece is a republished 2010 article, and the author notes some parts no longer hold up.
